scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 1 (Finite States), Chapter 8: Recursive Decision Processes. RDPs (Gamma, V, B), policy operators, well-posedness, global stability, greedy policies and the Bellman operator; Theorem 8.1.1 (optimality, HPI, OPI and VFI for globally stable RDPs) and Theorem 8.1.2 (well-posed bounded RDPs), proved here through a comparison property; nonstationary policies; topologically conjugate RDPs; examples (MDPs, cake eating, optimal stopping, Stokey-Lucas, state-dependent discounting, risk-sensitive, quantile and Epstein-Zin preferences, shortest paths); contracting RDPs with the error bound and Blackwell's condition, quantile job search and optimal default; eventually contracting RDPs and Proposition 6.2.2; convex and concave RDPs; adversarial agents, perturbed MDPs, robust control, KL penalties and the variational formula; Epstein-Zin RDPs; smooth ambiguity; minimization, shortest paths and negative discount rates; with the provable exercises.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 1: Finite States, Chapter 8, pp. 247-291.
